_purpose: Violations of a commercial gate that are ACCEPTED for now, each with an owner, a dated expiry, and the action that clears it.
_why: verify-wbs-chain.py is HARD: an unevidenced completion claim in the Agreed Specification is a contractual statement, so it must fail the gate. But this repository has one such violation TODAY, and a gate that is switched off because reality violates it is the gate-cannot-fail class (x6 in logs/known-failure-modes.md) arriving by the front door. So violations are not waived silently: they are enumerated here, owned, dated, and re-reported as warnings on every run. An exception missing an owner, an action or an expiry FAILS. An expired exception FAILS.
_not_a_waiver: An exception suppresses the FAIL, never the report. Every run still prints the violation with the exception cited against it.

exceptions.reason: WBS v0.5 marks task 0.4 'Done'. Its description names seven Dataverse tables plus an Anonymised Statistic snapshot; the solution holds Applicant, Application, Error Log, Setting and Grant. Review, Provider, Bank Account, Payment and the snapshot are absent. v0.5 is the customer-accepted specification (D-5), so its Status column cannot simply be edited — correcting it is a re-approval.
exceptions.clears_when: The five absent tables (Review, Provider, Bank Account, Payment, Anonymised Statistic) are built under tasks 6.4 and 8.1, which are Phase 3/Phase 4 work. There is no v0.6 to restate 0.4's status, so this cannot be cleared by correcting the document — only by building what the claim asserts.
exceptions.expiry_rationale: Phase 3 is contractually due 2026-11-27 and task 6.4 (Review table) sits in it. Previously 2026-09-30, chosen to force a v0.6 re-approval; with no v0.6 coming, the date that matters is the one by which the tables must exist.
exceptions.superseded_note: Original clearing action was 'WBS v0.6 restates 0.4 as Partially done'. The reviewer confirmed on 2026-08-19 that no v0.6 will be issued, so that route is closed.

exceptions.reason: The Grant Administration model-driven app is shipped and no WBS task names it. It is plainly implied by 0.4 (the solution and its tables) and by 2.2 (the Pending/Rejected/Borderline views, which need a surface), but the accepted specification never states it as a deliverable.
exceptions.clears_when: Add an evidence rule attributing rev_grantadministration to task 0.4 or 2.2, both of which imply it. With no v0.6 coming, naming it in the specification is not available.
exceptions.expiry_rationale: An evidence-map change is in our own hands and needs no re-approval, so the original date stands.
exceptions.superseded_note: Original clearing action assumed a WBS v0.6 could name the admin app. Confirmed 2026-08-19 that it cannot.

exceptions.matches: ready_but_client_blocked — DPO sign-off — tasks 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4 (incl. the rev_review table), 6.5
exceptions.reason: external-dependencies.json marks 'DPO sign-off' outstanding since 2026-07-04, blocking automations #0, #5 and #6. The reviewer (Xander Lykopoulos) directed building the trustee portal through access-test (WBS 6.1-6.5, including the rev_review table that task 6.4 creates) ahead of sign-off, and deferred automation #5 (narrative scrubbing, 5.1-5.7) for now — 6.1 formally depends_on 5.3, which this build does not wait for. Judged safe to build in DEV because: (a) the TAD Security Model already binds trustee visibility to rev_narrativeredacted, never rev_narrativeraw — the REV_TrusteeRestricted column-security profile built in Phase 1 keeps the raw narrative from ever reaching the trustee role regardless of automation #5's status, so the redacted field is simply unpopulated until #5 lands, not exposed; and (b) 6.5's access test uses synthetic/test data, not real applicant records.
exceptions.clears_when: DPO sign-off is received (clears the 'outstanding' state on 'DPO sign-off' in external-dependencies.json), and automation #5 (5.1-5.3) lands and releases narrative redaction before any live trustee demo (task 6.7) or production use — matching the handover's own recorded recommendation. Until both hold, the app stays in DEV with test data only; it is not shared with a real trustee against real applicant data.
exceptions.expiry_rationale: Automation #6 sits in Phase 3, contractually due 2026-11-27 — the same date EX-001 uses for the rev_review table this exception shares.

_no_v06_note: Both exceptions originally cleared via a WBS v0.6 re-approval. The reviewer confirmed on 2026-08-19 that no v0.6 will be issued. An exception whose clearing action can never happen is a permanent waiver, which C-COM-010 exists to prevent — so both were re-homed onto actions that are actually available.
